name: Bhairabi Temple
significance: A Shakta shrine at Kolibari near Tezpur overlooking the Brahmaputra and the Kolia Bhomora bridge, where Bhairavi is venerated as one of the Mahavidyas. Its stone carvings have been dated to the 9th century, and the structure has suffered earthquake damage.
story: Local tradition holds that Usha, daughter of the asura king Banasura, came regularly to this spot to worship the goddess.

name: Bhattarika Temple
significance: A riverside Shakti shrine on the bank of the Mahanadi at Sasanga in Baramba, Cuttack district, where the goddess Bhattarika is worshipped as a manifestation of Durga. Durga Puja is its principal annual observance.
story: Puranic tradition says the goddess appeared at this spot to lend Parashurama her power when he faced defeat at the hands of Sahasrarjuna.

name: Bhuvaneshwar Temple, Boudh
significance: A tenth-century Shiva temple at Malipara in Boudh town, on the right bank of the Mahanadi, raised under Somavamsi rule. Its walls carry khakhara-mundis and carved figures that include Ganesha alongside Jaina Tirthankaras.

name: Bhalei Mata Temple
builtDisplay: built by Raja Pratap Singh; date unrecorded
significance: A hill shrine in Bhalei village, Chamba district, built by Raja Pratap Singh and later renovated by Raja Sri Singh, whose sanctum holds a two-foot black stone image of the goddess. It draws large pilgrim gatherings at the Ashwin and Chait Navratris; the image was stolen in 1973 and recovered near Chohra.
story: The goddess is said to have appeared to Raja Pratap Singh in a dream asking to be brought out of a hidden place called Bhran, and the palanquin carrying her would move no further than Bhalei, which was read as her choice of site.

name: Cuttack Chandi Temple
significance: A Shakti shrine near the bank of the Mahanadi in Cuttack, dedicated to the goddess Chandi and counted among Odisha's principal goddess temples.

name: Bijasan Mata Temple
significance: A hilltop Devi temple on the edge of Indore, built in 1760 by Shivaji Rao Holkar and overlooking the city's airport. It draws thousands of pilgrims through Navaratri.

name: Biranchinarayan Temple, Palia
significance: A thirteenth-century sun temple at Palia in Bhadrak district, reconstructed in the early twentieth century by a local zamindar. Its sanctum holds a four-faced stone Surya image on a seven-horse chariot, and its eastern doorjambs appear to be reused from a 10th-11th century Shaiva temple.

name: Bhadrakali Temple, Aharapada
significance: A Shakti temple at Aharapada, some 8 km southwest of Bhadrak town, whose black granite goddess is seated in lotus posture on a lion.
story: Tradition holds that the image was first worshipped by the sage Tapasa Rushi in a cave on Meghasana hill in Mayurbhanj, and was carried to Aharapada by his disciples to keep it safe from Kalapahad.

name: Kurungaleeswarar Temple
significance: A medieval Shiva temple at Koyambedu on the bank of the Cooum in Chennai, dated to the twelfth-century Chola period and enclosing a large tank. The goddess is worshipped here as Dharmasamvardhini, and the temple tree is a jackfruit.
story: The shrine is said to have been developed by the sage Valmiki while Sita lived there after her separation from Rama, and is remembered as a place of family reunion after Rama was reunited with Lava and Kusha.

name: Lakhesvara Siva Temple
significance: A thirteenth-century rekha deula standing about 70 metres northeast of the Lingaraja temple in Bhubaneswar's Old Town, built on a saptaratha plan and enshrining a Shiva lingam set in a circular yoni-pitha.

name: Lakshmi Narasimhar Temple, Narasinghapuram
significance: A Vaishnava temple at Narasingapuram in Tiruvallur district that preserves fourteen inscriptions, twelve of them Vijayanagara, recording patronage by Achyuta Deva Raya in the 1530s and endowments as late as 1608. Its earliest records date to Kulothunga Chola I and Vikrama Chola.

name: Lakshminarasimha Temple, Haranhalli
significance: A three-shrined Hoysala temple at Haranhalli in Hassan district, completed in the 1230s at the expense of three brothers and now a protected monument of the Archaeological Survey of India. Its shrines house Venugopala, Keshava and Lakshminarasimha; originally dedicated to Kesava, it was later renamed for Lakshminarasimha.

name: Ganga Jadadisvarar Temple
significance: A Chola Shiva temple at Govindaputtur on the north bank of the Kollidam, built in 980 CE under Uttama Chola through his officer Ambalavan Paluvur Nakkan. It is counted among the Vaippu Sthalams and is praised in the Tevaram hymns of Appar and Sambandar.

name: Elai Kaatha Amman Temple
significance: A village goddess temple at Koyil Patti in the Kurichipatti panchayat of Madurai district, about 14 km from Melur, known chiefly for its annual festival cycle.
story: Local tradition treats Ezhai Kaatha Amman and the deity Valladikaarar as sister and brother, and their festivals are kept in relation to each other.

name: Madayi Kavu
significance: A hilltop Bhadrakali kavu at Madayi near Pazhayangadi in Kannur district, with four sanctums and worship in the Kaula tradition performed by Pidarar Brahmins. During Hyder Ali's incursion of 1780 the Nair warrior Vengayil Chathukutty is recorded as having defended it from desecration; it is now under the Malabar Devaswom Board.
story: The goddess is said to have slain the demon Darika, after which Shiva directed Parashurama to establish her shrine on this hill.

name: Ekambareswarar Temple, Chennai
significance: A Shiva temple on Mint Street in George Town, Chennai, built in the 1680s by Alanganatha Pillai, a dubash to the British East India Company. It appears on a 1710 map of Madras as 'Allingall's Pagoda' and stands among the Jain shrines and the Kandaswami temple of the same street.

name: Mahadeva Temple, Kalanjoor
significance: A Shiva temple at Kalanjoor in Pathanamthitta district, recorded as at least 1,100 years old, which carries the unusual feature of two adjacent copper-clad flagstaffs because both Mahadeva and Sastha are enshrined. Its 60-foot gopuram is approached by eighteen steps, and it lies about 80 km southwest of Sabarimala.

name: Elamgulam Sree Dharma Sastha Temple
builtDisplay: deity held to be c. 800 years old; renovated 2023
significance: A Sastha temple at Elamgulam in Kottayam district whose written history begins with its management by the Edappally royal family; control passed from the Nair Service Society to a wider committee in 1978. A major rebuilding in stone, wood and copper was completed in January 2023, and its annual Gajamela brings out some fifteen elephants.

name: Nedumpura Kulasekharanellur Shiva Temple
significance: One of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala, at Nedumpura in Thrissur district, distinguished by a sanctum built in the Gajaprishta form of an elephant's back. Krishna, Ganesha and Sastha are enshrined as subordinate deities.

name: Maa Bhangayani Temple, Haripurdhar
significance: A goddess temple at Haripurdhar in the Lesser Himalayan foothills of Sirmaur district, and one of the district's principal pilgrimage sites; it stays open to visitors year-round.
story: Tradition holds that Maa Bhangayani gave her blessing to Shirgul Maharaj, through which the king of Bagad and Guga Peer secured his release from Mughal captivity.

name: Iranikulam Mahadeva Temple
significance: One of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala, near Mala in Thrissur district, unusual in having two main shrines whose Shiva forms are worshipped as Thekkedathappan and Vadakkedathappan. Parvati and Subramanya are enshrined in the northern shrine.
story: The shrine is traditionally said to have been consecrated by the sage Parashurama.

name: Gajanan Maharaj Temple, Indore
significance: A temple to the Shegaon saint Gajanan Maharaj in Paliwal Nagar, Indore, begun in 1988 on land donated by Mr. Paliwal and completed in 1994 in Dholpur stone and marble. Its octagonal sanctum stands for the eight siddhis attributed to the saint, and the Thursday Mahaprasad, begun in 1992 with thirteen devotees, remains its central weekly rite.

name: Kottappuram Siva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Poothole in Thrissur, close to the Vadakkunnathan temple, counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala. Maha Shivaratri is its principal festival.
story: The temple is traditionally said to have been installed by the sage Parashurama.

name: Chakkamkulangara Siva Temple
significance: One of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala named in the Shivalaya Stotram, standing north of the Poornathrayeesa temple in Thrippunithura, the old Brahmin settlement that served as the Cochin kingdom's capital. It is unusual in also carrying a full Navagraha installation.
story: The lingam is traditionally said to have been installed by the sage Parashurama.

name: Eravikulangara Temple
significance: A temple at Akaparambu in Ernakulam district where the Devi is the principal deity alongside Shiva and Sastha. A Thambula Prasna held in 2007 led to the installation of Brahmarakshas and Naga shrines the following year.
story: The goddess is said to owe her strength to the Brahmachari scholar Sankara Sarma, who moved his household worship of Bhadrakali to this temple before renouncing the world.

name: Maa Simsa Temple
significance: A shrine to Sharada Devi at Simsa village in the Ladbharol area of Joginder Nagar subdivision, Mandi district, drawing its largest gatherings at Navratri; a second temple to the same goddess stands at Daroh near Palampur.

name: Durga Mandir, Ramnagar
significance: A square stone Durga temple at Ramnagar, Varanasi, raised by Maharaja Balwant Singh of Banaras. Much of it was destroyed by British cannon fire when Warren Hastings sent troops to seize Raja Chait Singh, and it was afterwards rebuilt to the original design; it remains under the Banaras royal family.
story: The shrine is said to have been dedicated to Vishnu at first and turned over to Durga after unexplained happenings in its compound.

name: Lodheshwar Mahadev Mandir
significance: A Shiva temple on the bank of the Ghaghra at Mahadeva village in Barabanki district, whose lingam is reckoned among the rarest of the 52 associated with the Shakti Pithas. It is the kuldevta shrine of the Lodhi Rajputs, and a well beside it is known as the Pandav-Kup.
story: Tradition says that when Parashurama was destroying the kshatriyas, the surviving Lodhis appealed to their deity, who told them to lay down weapons and take up the tools of agriculture.

name: Durga Devi Temple, Guhagar
significance: A Durga temple in the coastal town of Guhagar, Ratnagiri district, laid out on the panchayatana plan with four corner shrines around the central sanctum, and set beside a tank with a wooden pillar at its centre.
story: The goddess is said to have destroyed the forces menacing Guhagar and slain the demon Mahishasura, and is worshipped here as Mahishasuramardini.

name: Mahadeva Temple, Avittathur
significance: A Shiva temple at Avittathur in Thrissur district, counted among the sixty-four ancient Brahmin settlements of Kerala and protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. The Avittathur inscription of AD 1024 records grants of paddy land for its upkeep under the Cheras.
story: The lingam is traditionally said to have been installed by Parashurama, with the sage Agastya laying out the temple and fixing its daily rites.

name: Malayalappuzha Devi Temple
significance: A Bhadrakali temple at Malayalappuzha in Pathanamthitta district whose 5.5-foot image is made in katu-sarkara-yogam and shows the goddess in her fierce form; the sanctum holds three images, used respectively for worship, abhisheka and sreebali. Its consecration is credited to the Aikireth and Eravimangalath Namboothiri families, and its eleven-day festival opens on Thiruvathira in Kumbham.
story: Two Namboothiri pilgrims are said to have been directed by Bhadrakali herself to enshrine her at Malayalappuzha as the most auspicious place.

name: Garh Ganesh Temple
significance: A hill temple on the Aravalli ridge above Jaipur, founded by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, the city's founder, in connection with an Ashvamedha yajna. Its Ganesha is shown without a trunk, an uncommon form, and the shrine is reached by 365 steps standing for the days of the year.

name: Durga Temple, Motia
significance: A tenth-century Kalinga temple near Krushnaprasad in Cuttack district whose four-armed goddess is shown slaying Mahishasura with conch and discus in her upper hands. Sculptures recovered from the site by the Archaeological Survey of India place its origin in the Somavamsi period, with eight-armed Durga pieces comparable to those at the Vaital temple.

name: Eri-Katha Ramar Temple
significance: One of the oldest Rama temples in South India, at Maduranthakam in Chengalpattu district, counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshetrams of Vaishnavism and endowed by the Chola king Parantaka I. Ramanuja is held to have received his Pancha Samskaram here beneath the temple's magizha tree.
story: The temple's name is traced to 1798, when the British Collector Lionel Blaze is said to have seen Rama and Lakshmana standing as warriors on the bunds of the tank as it threatened to breach in the monsoon.

name: Durga Temple, Baideshwar
significance: An eighth-century shrine at Baideshwar in Cuttack district built as a khakhara vimana in the early Kalinga manner, comparable to the Vaital Deula and the Varahi Deula at Chaurasi. Besides the eight-armed Durga it houses images of Parvati, Aja-Ekapada Bhairava and Ganesha.

name: Duladeo Temple
significance: The last of the Chandela temples at Khajuraho, standing by the Khodar river and dedicated to Shiva, whose name means 'holy bridegroom'. It is a nirandhara temple on the seven-chariot plan, one of the twenty-two Shiva shrines of the group inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

name: Ganapati Temple, Redi
builtDisplay: shrine raised after the idol's discovery in 1976
significance: A Ganesha shrine at Redi in coastal Maharashtra, about 30 km from Vengurla, built around an image dug out of the shore near Rewati port in 1976. The idol stands roughly 6 ft high and is dwibhuja, two-armed rather than the usual four; the mouse that serves as his vahana was found two months later.
story: A local man, Sadashiv Kambli, is said to have seen the buried Ganesha in a dream and persuaded villagers to dig it out of the seashore.

name: Gajanan Maharaj Temple, Kanhor
significance: A temple to the Shegaon saint Gajanan Maharaj at Kanhor in Kulgaon-Badlapur, Thane district, opened on Vijaya Dashami in 1981 on land given free by Vitthalrao Raut. Its Seva Samiti dates from the same year and has kept the Prakat Din Utsav annually since.
story: The temple is said to have been begun after the devotee Shripadrao Kulkarni was directed to it in a dream, and an audumbar tree that sprang up beside the chosen site was taken as a sign.

name: Garbharakshambigai Temple
deity: Shiva as Mullaivananathar, with Parvati as Garbharakshambigai
significance: A Shiva temple at Thirukarukavur in Thanjavur district, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams sung in the Tevaram and one of the five Pancha Aranya forest shrines of the Kumbakonam country. Thirty-one inscriptions record land grants by Rajaraja I, Rajendra Chola I and Kulothunga Chola.
story: The goddess is said to have shielded a pregnant woman's unborn child in a pot after an angry sage cursed it, which is why she is invoked as the protector of the womb.

name: Perakam Mahadeva Temple
significance: One of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala and among the oldest in Thrissur district, at Perakam village, with a round sreekovil set within a nalambalam alongside a thidappalli and mandapam. Maha Shivaratri is its chief festival.
story: Folklore holds that the sage Parashurama installed the Shiva image at Perakam.

name: Deulajhari
significance: An old Shaiva centre in Athmallik subdivision, Angul district, where the Siddheswar Baba temple stands within some 24 acres of native pandanus forest. Twenty-four hot springs survive on the site, out of eighty-four recorded there in the past.

name: EME Temple
significance: A temple built in February 1966 on the Indian Army's EME School campus at Vadodara under its first commandant, Brigadier A. F. Eugene, its aluminium geodesic dome following Buckminster Fuller's design. It draws architectural motifs from six faiths as a statement of Indian secularism and holds 108 stone sculptures dated between about 600 and 1600 CE.

name: Madhav Govind Rameshwar Temple
significance: A trikutachala shrine at Agapur in Ponda taluka, Goa, whose three sanctums hold Vaishnava and Shaiva deities together.

name: Ramnathi Temple
significance: A Goud Saraswat Brahmin temple at Bandora in Ponda, moved here from Loutolim in 1566 to save it from destruction under Portuguese rule and largely rebuilt in 1905. It follows the panchayatana arrangement with five shrines, the older Betal and Kalbhairav structures having been kept from before the rebuilding; the temple marked 450 years on the site in May 2011.
story: The lineage of the deity is traced to Rama, who is said to have installed a Shivalinga at Rameswaram in expiation for the killing of the brahmin Ravana.
